questions.stem:
GitHub Copilot cloud agent must call an internal API documentation service at `docs.api.contoso.com` while it works on issues. The session log shows the request was blocked by the firewall. Security requires that the agent can still reach only approved destinations.

What should you do?

options.text: Disable the cloud agent firewall for the repository.
options.rationale: Incorrect. This removes the control entirely, so the agent could reach any destination.

options.text: Store the service URL as an Agents variable.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A variable passes a value to the agent; it doesn't change which hosts the firewall allows.

options.text: Add `docs.api.contoso.com` to the firewall's custom allowlist in the repository's Copilot cloud agent settings.
options.rationale: Correct. It opens exactly one approved destination and keeps every other host blocked.

options.text: Tell the agent in `copilot-instructions.md` that the domain is trusted.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Instructions can't open a connection the firewall blocks.

questions.explanation: The firewall limits the agent's outbound access to an allowlist. Widen it by the one host you need instead of removing the control.
questions.takeaway: Blocked by the firewall → allowlist the specific host; never disable the firewall.

questions.stem:
You create `.github/agents/reviewer.agent.md` for a review-only agent. The frontmatter contains `name` and `description`, but no `tools` property. During testing, the agent edits files and runs shell commands.

Why?

options.text: When `tools` is omitted, the custom agent can use all available tools.
options.rationale: Correct. An omitted `tools` list means all tools. List only read and search tools to make it review-only.

options.text: Custom agents always inherit the tools of the agent that invoked them.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A custom agent's own `tools` property defines its tools; here it's missing, so the default (all) applies.

options.text: The `description` must contain the words "read-only" to restrict tools.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The description explains the agent's purpose; it doesn't restrict tools.

options.text: Tool restrictions only apply to files named `*.instructions.md`.
options.rationale: Incorrect. `.instructions.md` files are custom instructions, not agents, and have no `tools` property.

questions.explanation: Restrict a custom agent's capabilities in its frontmatter. Leaving `tools` out grants everything.

questions.stem:
CODEOWNERS assigns `/infra/` to `@contoso/platform`. An agent's pull request that changes only `infra/main.bicep` was merged after one approval from a developer who isn't on the platform team. The ruleset on `main` requires one approving review.

What should you change so that this can't happen again?

options.text: Move the `/infra/` line above the `*` line in CODEOWNERS.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The last matching pattern wins, so placing it above `*` makes `*` override it.

options.text: Increase the required approving reviews to two.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Both approvals could still come from people who don't own `/infra/`.

options.text: Enable "Dismiss stale pull request approvals when new commits are pushed".
options.rationale: Incorrect. That reacts to new commits; it doesn't require the owner's review.

options.text: Enable "Require review from Code Owners" in the ruleset.
options.rationale: Correct. Without this rule, CODEOWNERS only requests reviewers; with it, an owner of each changed path must approve.

questions.explanation: CODEOWNERS on its own only requests reviews. The ruleset's code owner review rule is what blocks the merge.

questions.stem:
A public repository tests pull requests with a workflow that uses `on: pull_request_target`, checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha`, and runs `dotnet test` with `NUGET_TOKEN` from secrets. A pull request from a fork exfiltrated `NUGET_TOKEN`.

You need to keep testing pull requests from forks while preventing this. What should you do?

options.text: Keep `pull_request_target`, but add `permissions: contents: read`.
options.rationale: Incorrect. A read-only token doesn't stop the fork's code reading secrets passed to the job.

options.text: Change the trigger to `pull_request`, so fork pull requests run without secrets and with a read-only token.
options.rationale: Correct. `pull_request` withholds secrets from forks and caps the token at read, so untrusted code has nothing to steal.

options.text: Rotate `NUGET_TOKEN` every week.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Rotation limits how long a stolen token is useful; it doesn't prevent the theft.

options.text: Move `NUGET_TOKEN` to an organisation secret.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The job still receives the secret, so the fork's code can still read it.

questions.explanation: `pull_request_target` runs in the base repository's context with secrets. Checking out and running a fork's code there hands those secrets to the attacker (a "pwn request").
questions.takeaway: Untrusted PR code → `pull_request`; never run fork code under `pull_request_target`.

questions.stem:
You write a GitHub Agentic Workflow that triages new issues. The agent may add one comment and labels from an approved list, and nothing else. Prompt injection in issue text is a concern.

How should you configure the workflow?

options.text: Give the workflow `issues: write` and list the allowed labels in the Markdown instructions.
options.rationale: Incorrect. With write access, an injected instruction could make the agent close issues or use any label; instructions aren't enforced.

options.text: Run the agent with `permissions: write-all` and review its actions in the logs afterwards.
options.rationale: Incorrect. Reviewing afterwards doesn't prevent damage, and `write-all` breaks least privilege.

options.text: Add a `preToolUse` hook that asks the user before each write.
options.rationale: Incorrect. The run is non-interactive, so there is nobody to ask; this doesn't express the allowed outputs.

options.text: Keep the agent read-only and declare `add-comment` (max 1) and `add-labels` with the allowed labels as safe outputs.
options.rationale: Correct. The agent only proposes; a separate deterministic job validates the proposal against the declared types and limits and holds the write permission.

questions.explanation: Safe outputs separate proposing from executing. The agent never holds write permission, and anything outside the declared outputs is rejected.
questions.takeaway: Agent proposes, safe-output job decides and writes.
